name: Chernobyl Ant
imitates: A buggy foam terrestrial that suggests a big ant, beetle or stonefly and floats a dropper nymph in summer.
recipe: 3 mm black foam over 2 mm yellow foam

steps.text: Start the thread behind the eye and wrap back to the bend. Cut a black and a yellow foam strip about as wide as the hook gap, with the ends notched to a point.
Lay the black foam on the hook and tie it in at the bend.
Lay the yellow strip on top of the black, overlapping at the rear, and tie it down with several tight wraps.
Tie one rubber leg on each side of the hook at the foam tie-down point.
Push the foam out of the way, tie in a rooster saddle feather by its butt, then tie in a length of chenille at the base of the foam.
Wrap the chenille forward to the eye, tie it off and clip the excess.
Palmer the hackle heavily up the hook to the front, tie it off and clip it.
Fold the black foam forward over the body and tie it down behind the eye with a couple of tight wraps.
Fold the yellow foam over the top of the black and tie it down on top of it.
Tie one rubber leg in on each side of the fly at the front.
Trim the front of the foam straight across, lift it, and whip finish behind the eye.
The finished Chernobyl Ant: black foam body with a yellow top, hackled underbody and rubber legs.
